summary: The candidate is a substantive partial fix: it plumbs typed kv_events_config/page_size/dp_size into the rebuilt Rust extension, adds the kv_events field, preserves the existing allowlist/redaction boundary, and passes its focused Rust serialization tests plus the Python route contract suite. It does not fully meet the safe-advertisement/parity contract because its hand-written TCP parser accepts malformed bracketed non-IPv6 hosts that Python's canonical parser rejects, causing Rust to advertise metadata where the contract requires null.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before comparison on the exact recorded base: the Rust /server_info serializer has no kv_events field.

On the exact candidate, the real Python /server_info handler contract passed: 29 tests and 12 subtests, covering valid, disabled, malformed, endpoint/port/page-size, IPv6, and field-preservation cases.

tests.what_was_measured: Compiled the changed Rust crate at candidate commit c5812a14220bf0d4ebe1cf98cd2c63b818c98aa8 with pinned rustc 1.92.0 and ran the candidate's four focused serializer, null-fallback, IPv6, and redaction tests; all passed.

Forced a release rebuild from /job/repo/rust and imported the resulting candidate-native extension from /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a64e132cdd59/rust-extension-cache/artifacts/sglang-server/2ea160b8752586fa96c77fddaa174c3025dc3e11c1da99c5cf38336b0c42daae/_server.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so; ServerArgs exposed kv_events_config, page_size, and dp_size.

Independent temporary adversarial test (removed immediately afterward): Python parse_advertisable_tcp('tcp://[not-ipv6]:5557') returns None, but candidate Rust returned Some(('[not-ipv6]', 5557)), violating malformed-endpoint null behavior and Python parity.

gpu_evidence: No GPU execution was needed or performed. This change is CPU-side PyO3/Rust HTTP metadata parsing and serialization; it changes no model kernels. The prepared environment is x86_64 Linux with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2, which were left unchanged.
remaining_counterexamples: kv_events_config={"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://[not-ipv6]:5557","topic":"kv"}, page_size=64, dp_size=1: Python declines advertisement (null), while candidate Rust advertises endpoint_host='[not-ipv6]' and endpoint_port_base=5557.
remaining_limitations: The exact candidate's rebuilt Rust library and internal serializer were exercised, but a live Rust HTTP server was not started because this metadata-only review had no model-weight prerequisite and the deterministic tiny-Llama fixture would only add transport/engine smoke coverage; no candidate Axum route-level regression test was supplied.

The candidate uses a bespoke Rust endpoint parser rather than the Python NetworkAddress semantics, so malformed endpoint parity beyond the demonstrated bracketed-host counterexample remains under-specified and should receive a shared matrix test.
KV-event publishing itself is intentionally out of scope and was not exercised.

The host image initially lacked cargo/rustc. Rust 1.92.0 was installed into an isolated job-local toolchain and all Cargo targets/caches stayed outside the checkout; the frozen GPU software stack was not changed.
